Now I should check if this works. The issue specifically mentioned `xdg-open`.
I can try to create a test case that mocks `subprocess.Popen` and checks if `.wait()` is called when `wait=False`.

Since I cannot create new test files, I'll use a python script to verify.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import subprocess
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
import typer

# Mocking the environment to simulate Linux/BSD and xdg-open presence
with patch("typer.main._is_macos", return_value=False), \
     patch("typer.main._is_linux_or_bsd", return_value=True), \
     patch("shutil.which", return_value="/usr/bin/xdg-open"), \
     patch("subprocess.Popen") as mock_popen:
    
    mock_process = MagicMock()
    mock_popen.return_value = mock_process
    
    # Test wait=False
    result = typer.launch("https://google.com", wait=False)
    assert result == 0
    mock_process.wait.assert_not_called()
    
    # Reset mock
    mock_process.wait.reset_mock()
    
    # Test wait=True
    mock_process.wait.return_value = 0
    result = typer.launch("https://google.com", wait=True)
    assert result == 0
    mock_process.wait.assert_called_once()

print("Tests passed!")
EOF
